tem1: Is your walk really brisk? 100 steps a minute marks moderate intensity. A metronome that plays a step sound at your chosen pace, a 15-second pace check and weekly tracking.
tem3: Is your walk really “brisk”? Research shows that about 100 steps a minute corresponds to moderate-intensity exercise. This metronome plays a sound for every step at the pace you choose, and you match your steps to it. First you can count how many steps you take in 15 seconds to check your pace today.

tem53: In two laboratory studies in the US (adults aged 21–40 and 41–60), walking at about 100 steps a minute corresponded to moderate intensity (3 METs) and about 130 steps a minute to vigorous intensity (6 METs). Each increase of 10 steps means roughly 1 MET more effort. Counting your steps is a practical way to tell whether your walk is “brisk”.
tem54: Is this pace the same for everyone?
tem55: No. These figures are averages for healthy adults and vary from person to person. For someone with lower fitness, older age or higher body weight, 100 steps a minute may be harder. Start at a pace that feels comfortable and build up gradually. If you have heart disease, or if you get chest pain, dizziness or breathlessness that stops you talking while walking, stop and talk to your doctor.
tem56: Does it work with my phone in my pocket?
tem57: While the page is open, the screen is kept from switching off, which keeps the sounds going. On some phones, the sound may pause if the screen locks or you switch to another app. It works best with the sound on and the screen left on while you carry the phone in your pocket.
tem58: How much should I walk each week?
tem59: The World Health Organization recommends that adults do at least 150–300 minutes of moderate-intensity or 75–150 minutes of vigorous-intensity aerobic activity a week. You can meet this with 30 minutes of brisk walking on 5 days a week; shorter walks count too.
